dedupe_keys.name: india5g open source 4g and 5g universal broadband techno economic model using remote sensing

description: This open-source codebase tests 4G and 5G strategies for universal broadband, combining remote sensing with least-cost network design, and was published with an IEEE Access paper of 2021 by Edward Oughton and Ashutosh Jha. The model estimates demand from population and income layers derived from satellite and census data, designs the least-cost radio access and backhaul needed to meet a target speed in each area, and computes the financial cost and the private and government shares of cost for different technologies, spectrum prices and backhaul options, reporting for example the cost per smartphone connected. Applied to India, the world's second largest mobile market with very high spectrum prices, it shows the trade-offs between technology choices and argues that current infrastructure policy, especially fibre backhaul, decides whether 6G-grade service can later be delivered; the authors state the code can be applied to any country. Coverage: India in the paper, with a design for any country. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10.1109/access.2021.3097627) is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: many cost and demand assumptions; spatial units are coarse (sub-regional). Simulation uses: capacity planning and cost optimisation of national broadband roll-out, and policy scenarios such as spectrum pricing and infrastructure sharing. Related records: pysim5g is the earlier techno-economic simulator from the same author, and the ITU and World Bank broadband resources give inputs.
